title: Deriving the ordinary subsequence extension
statement:
The ordinary additive subsequence extension sends quasi-isomorphisms between strict complexes with all components flat-term independently K-flat to quasi-isomorphisms. Consequently it has a normalized everywhere-defined pointwise universal left derived functor, with the ordinary functor and adjunction retained exactly, comparison invertible on this resolving class, exact triangulated structure, shift compatibility, and adjunction to derived subsequence restriction.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v w
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  [EssentiallySmall.{w} C]
  [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
  (S : SystemScalarAssignment (J := J)) (T : SystemTensorCoherence S)
  (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (r : ℕ ↪o ℕ)
def systemSelectedDerivedExtension (S : SystemScalarAssignment (J := J))
    (T : SystemTensorCoherence S) :
    SystemDerivedLeftExtension (systemSubsequence B r)
      (systemComponentwiseKFlat (selectedSystemRings B r))
```

proof.text: At each level the ordinary comparison identifies the extended map with scalar extension of the corresponding selected component. Independent K-flat change of rings preserves its quasi-isomorphism. Componentwise detection gives a quasi-isomorphism of systems. Simultaneous flat-term K-flat representatives resolve every strict complex, so apply the general normalized resolving-class left extension theorem.
